title: I used Astra to build a voice-controlled D&D-style game in half a day
author: Intelligent_Key2760
selftext:
Really impressed with GPT-6 Astra. I put this prototype together in roughly half a day.

It's a voice-controlled game where you talk to a virtual Dungeon Master, tell it what you want to do, and see where the story goes, with key moments turned into AI generated video scenes.

At important moments, like crossing a broken bridge or negotiating with a dragon, the DM asks for a d20 check. The game handles the roll and modifiers, then the DM narrates what happens next.

I used GPT-6 Astra to build and iterate on the prototype, Agora for voice interaction, and Reactor's MiniMax FastH3 for the generated video. After a major dice check, the outcome is turned into a short scene.

The attached recording shows the current version. Skip to around 1:03 if you want to see the generated video.

There's still work to do on video latency and visual consistency. The main issue right now is pacing: the generated video doesn't start playing until the DM finishes speaking. If I were playing, I wouldn't want to wait that long either lol.

Still, I'm surprised by how much came together in one afternoon. I'll keep polishing it.

comments.author: nickick_
comments.body: Are you running FastH3 on a provider like Modal? How are you handling startup times for the video GPUs?

replies.author: Intelligent_Key2760
replies.body: Sorry, I don't have a good answer on that yet. I'm running FastH3 on Reactor for now because I wanted to get the MVP working first.
